questions.question: If Sonu is driving a car at a speed of 20 m/s, then in how much time Sonu will cover a distance of 936 km?
questions.solution:
**Given****:**

Sonu is driving a car at a speed of 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h; 

Distance = 936 km

**Formula Used****:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation****:**

Using the above formulae, we have

⇒ Time = 936/72 = 13 hr

∴ Sonu will cover 936 km in 13 hours.

questions.question: The height of a cone is 16 cm and radius of its base is 30 cm. If the rate of painting it is Rs. 14/cm², then what will be the total cost in painting the curved surface area of cone from outside?
questions.solution:
**Given****:**

The height of a cone is 16 cm and the radius of its base is 30 cm.

**Formula Used****:**

l² = r² + h²; 

The curved surface area of the cone = π × r × l

Where r, h and l are radius, height and slant height respectively

**Calculation****:**

Using the above formulae, we have

⇒ l² = (16² + 30²)

⇒ l = √{256 + 900}

⇒ l = √{1156}

⇒ l = 34 cm

∴ The total cost of painting the curved surface area of the cone from outside 

⇒ 22/7 × 34 × 30 × 14 =** Rs. 44880**

questions.question: The average weight of a group of 22 students increases by 1 kg when the weight of the teacher is also included. If the initial average weight of the group of 22 students was 31 kg, then what is the weight of the teacher?
questions.solution:
**Given****:** 

The average weight of a group of 22 students increases by 1 kg when the weight of the teacher is also included.

**Formula Used****:** 

Average = (sum of terms)/(number of terms)

**Calculation****:** 

Let the weight of the teacher be ‘y’ kg

Initial average weight of the group of 22 students = 31 kg

Average weight of a group of (22 students + teacher) = 32 kg

According to the question,

⇒ (31 × 22 + y)/23 = 32 

⇒ y = 736 – 682 = 54 kg

∴ Weight of the teacher = 54 kg,

questions.question: The price of two articles are in the ratio of 3 : 2 respectively. The price of first article is increased by 40% and the price of second article is decreased by x%. If the new ratio of the price of the two articles is 7 : 3 respectively, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
**Given****:**

The price of two articles are in the ratio of 3 : 2 respectively

**Formula Used****:**

Selling price = Cost price + profit

Selling price = Cost price – loss

**Calculation****:**

Let the cost price of two articles be 3y and 2y respectively, then

When the price of first article is increased by 40%

Price of first article = 3y + (40/100) × 3y = 4.2y 

When the price of second article is decreased by x%

Price of second article = 2y – (x/100) × 2y = 2y – 2xy/100

Now,

⇒ (4.2y)/(2y – 2xy/100) = 7 : 3

⇒ 12.6y = 14y – 14xy/100

⇒ 14xy/100 = 1.4y

⇒ x = 10%

∴ Value of x is 10

When the price of first article is increased by 40%

When the price of second article is decreased by x%

Price of second article = 200y(1 – (x/100))

As per the question,

frac{{420y}}{{200y( {1 - (x)/({100)}} )}} = (7)/(3)

frac{{180}}{{200}} = ( {1 - (x)/({100)}} )

x = 10

questions.question: A bag has Rs. 420 in the denomination of Rs. 1, Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 coins. The number Rs. 1, Rs. 2 and Rs. 5 coins are in the ratio of 8 : 1 : 5. How many coins of Rs. 5 are in the bag?
questions.solution:

A bag has Rs. 420 in the denomination of Rs. 1, Rs. 2, and Rs. 5 coins

Ratio of coins of Rs. 1, Rs. 2, and Rs. 5 = 8 ∶ 1 ∶ 5

**Calculation****:** 

Let the number of Rs. 1, Rs. 2, and Rs. 5 be 8y, y, 5y.

Also, it has a total of Rs. 420

⇒ 8y + 2(y) + 5 × (5y) = 420

⇒ 8y + 2y + 25y = 420 

⇒ 35y = 420 

⇒ y = 12

Number of coins of Rs. 5 in the bag = 5y = 60

**∴ The number of coins of Rs. 5 in the bag is 60.**

questions.question: If P is 40% less than Q, then Q is how much percentage more than P?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P is 40% less than Q.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

40% = 2/5

So, Q is 2/(5-2) × 100 = 2/3 × 100 = 66.66% more than P.

∴ Q is 66.66% more than P.

**Calculation:**

Let, Q = 100y

So, P = 100y × (100 - 40)/100 = 100y × 60/100 = 60y

Now,

(Q – P)/P × 100 = 40y/60y × 100 = 66.66%

**∴ Q is 66.66% more than P.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

If A is 20% less than B,

So,

B is 20/(100 - 20) × 100 = 20/80 × 100 = 25% more than A

Similarly,

If B is 25% more than A,

So,

A is 25/(100 + 25) × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20% less than B.

u : v = 9 × 4 : 9 × 7 = 36 : 63 ----(i)

v : w = 9 × 7 : 7 × 7 = 63 : 49 ----(ii)

So, Equating the ratios we get,

u ∶ v ∶ w = 36 ∶ 63 ∶ 49

⇒ u ∶ w = 36 ∶ 49

When u = 72, 

⇒ w = 49 × 72/36 = 98

**∴ Value of w is 98**

questions.question: A sum becomes 5 times of itself in 3 years. at compound interest (interest is compounded annually). In how many years. will the sum becomes 125 times of itself?
questions.solution:
**Given****:** 

A sum becomes 5 times of itself in 3 years. at compound interest (interest is compounded annually).

**Formula Used****:** 

When calculate at compound interest 

Amount (A) = p (1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where p, r, and n respectively are principal, rate of interest, and time

**Calculation****:** 

Let the sum be p 

Rate be r%

According to the question,

5p = p(1 + r/100)³

⇒ 5 = (1 + r/100)³ ...i)

Let the sum becomes 125 times in n years. 

125p = p(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ 125 = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ (5)³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ ...ii)

Comparing equation (ii) with (i) we get,

n = 9

**∴ In 9 years it will become 125 times.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a63c93e11c1bd5840d125804b189a0e6fab4be6ad12b4d33c13eace1e72ac42b.png] ** **

A certain sum at C.I becomes ‘y’ times in n₁ years. and ‘z’ times in n₂ years. then y¹/n₁ = z¹/n₂****

Using the above formulae, we have

⇒ 5¹/³ = 125¹/n₂

⇒ 5¹/³ = 5³/n₂

⇒ n₂ = 9 years.

**∴ The sum becomes 125 times of itself in 9 years.**

questions.question: If the average of five observations a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ and a₅ is N, then what is the average of five new observations a₁ − 100, a₂ − 100, a₃ − 100, a₄ − 100, and a₅ − 100
questions.solution:
**Calculation****:**

Using the above formulae, we have

Average of a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ and a₅ is N 

Sum of a₁, a₂, a₃, a₄ and a₅ is 5N 

Sum of (a₁ – 100 + a₂ – 100 + a₃ – 100 + a₄ – 100 + a₅ – 100) = 5N – 500

Average = {5N – (100 + 100 + 100 + 100 + 100)}/5

Average = {(N × 5) – (100 × 5)}/5 = N – 100

∴ Required average = N – 100

questions.question: Anil, Deepak and Dinesh together can complete a work in 35 days. Anil and Dinesh together can complete the same work in 60 days. In how many days Deepak alone can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given****:**

Anil, Deepak and Dinesh together can complete a work in 35 days.

Anil and Dinesh together can complete the same work in 60 days 

**Calculation****:**

Let Deepak alone can complete the same work in ‘y’ days

Work done by Deepak in 1 day = 1/y units 

Anil and Dinesh together can complete the same work in 60 days

Work done by Anil and Dinesh in 1 day = 1/60 units

⇒ 1/60 + 1/y = 1/35

⇒ 35 × (y + 60) = 60y

⇒ 25y = 2100

⇒ y = 84 days

∴ Deepak alone can complete the same work in 84 days.
